rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's description: its fruits resembled jars and leaves elephant ears; when covered by God's command, it became ruby, emerald, and similar things.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «انتهيت إلى السدرة فإذا نبقها مثل الجرار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report through Anas and Malik ibn Sasaa, the Prophet describes reaching the seventh heaven, meeting Abraham, then seeing Sidra fruit like Hajar pitchers and leaves like elephant ears.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن أنس بن مالك، عن مالك بن صعصعة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet rode al-Buraq to the Sidra; its leaves were like elephant ears and fruit like pitchers, then its beauty became indescribable as God covered it and revealed what He revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ركبت البراق ثم ذهب بي إلى سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that an angel carried the Prophet to the Sidra; he recognized its leaves and fruit, but divine covering transformed it beyond description.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عرج بي الملك» ؛ قال: «ثم انتهيت إلى السدرة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة، أو غيره
rows.claim: A report whose attribution is uncertain (Abu Hurayra or another) says the Sidra marks the limit for each follower of the Prophet's Sunnah; rivers of pure water, milk, wine, and honey flow from it, and its vast shade and leaf encompass the ummah.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أو غيره شك أبو جعفر الرازي

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Sidra as at the center of Paradise, with abundant silk and brocade upon it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr reports the Prophet said a hundred riders could travel or take shade beneath one branch; it contains golden moths and pitcher-like fruit.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وذكر سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas describes a tree whose shade takes a rider a hundred years to cross and whose leaf covers the entire community.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع، عن {سدرة المنتهى}

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's description of the Sidra in the seventh heaven: its fruit is like Hajar pitchers and its leaves like elephant ears; two rivers emerge openly and two are hidden, which Gabriel identifies as the Nile and Euphrates and rivers of Paradise respectively.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {عند سدرة المنتهى} [النجم: 14] : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that angels are female is the full extent of the unbelievers' knowledge: disbelief, shirk, and conjecture without certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: بالله، والشرك به على وجه الظن بغير يقين علم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says their knowledge goes no further than rejecting the Messenger and plotting against what came from God; they are the people of shirk.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gave the man who reproached him a little of the money he had promised, then withheld the remainder out of miserliness.
rows.anchor: وعن دينه، وأعطى صاحبه قليلا من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported occasion of revelation identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after following the Prophet, he was promised that a reproacher would bear his afterlife punishment if he returned to shirk; he returned, paid part, then withheld the rest.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن هذه الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة من أجل أنه عاتبه بعض المشركين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who gave a little and then stopped.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وأكدى}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that a newly converted man was pressured to return to his fathers' religion; a reproacher offered to bear his punishment for payment, demanded more, and obtained a written agreement witnessed by others.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أفرأيت الذي تولى}

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the man gave a little and then stopped.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أعطى قليلا وأكدى} [النجم: 34] قال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains akda as stopping the gift; he compares it to a well that has struck hard ground and stopped yielding, supporting the sense of cessation.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وأعطى قليلا وأكدى} [النجم: 34]

rows.speaker: ابن طاوس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Tawus and Qatada say the man gave a little, then cut off the gift.
rows.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، وقتادة، في قوله: {وأكدى}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima gives the same explanation: he gave a little, then stopped.
rows.anchor: ثنا معمر، عن عكرمة، مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the man was miserly and stopped his giving.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأكدى} [النجم: 34]

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the man's giving stopped.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وأكدى} [النجم: 34]

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses akda as making terms difficult or bargaining hard; Arabic usage describes digging until hard ground is met, nails becoming rough, fingers tiring, and a plant yielding little.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله : {وأكدى}

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
rows.claim: Some Arab linguists derive akda from a well's hard stratum: the digger reaches it and despairs of finding water.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب يقول: اشتق قوله: أكدى، من كدية الركية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham completed obedience through what he did with his son after the dream; the scrolls of Moses state that no bearer bears another's burden, through the rest of the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says Abraham fulfilled his duty by being ready to sacrifice his son.
rows.anchor: عن القرظي، وسئل، عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another reported view is that Abraham fulfilled all the ordinances of Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون بل معنى ذلك: أنه وفى ربه جميع شرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Islam has thirty portions, no one tested by this religion established it as Abraham did, and God granted him exemption from the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: «الإسلام ثلاثون سهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Abraham fulfilled what was prescribed for him.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وإبراهيم الذي وفى}

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God named Abraham His intimate friend because morning and evening he recited the verse beginning فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون, through its end.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن معاذ بن أنس

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view says Abraham fulfilled his Lord's work for the day; a report from Abu Umama has the Prophet explain that he performed four daytime rakahs.
rows.anchor: ذكر من قال ذلك: حدثنا أبو كريب قال: ثنا الحسن بن عطية قال: ثنا إسرائيل، عن جعفر بن الزبير، عن القاسم، عن أبي أمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari prefers that Abraham fulfilled all the ordinances of Islam and every commanded act of obedience, because the report about his fulfillment is general and does not single out one act.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: وفى جميع شرائع الإسلام وجميع ما أمر به من الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that no bearer bears another's burden is cited as material in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, not as a restriction defining what Abraham fulfilled.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك مما أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه في صحف موسى وإبراهيم، لا مما خص به الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari says he would follow either prophetic report if sound, but their chains raise concerns that require verification.
rows.anchor: ولكن في إسنادهما نظر يجب التثبت فيهما من أجله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that at Mina the moon split, one part going behind a mountain, and the Prophet told the people to bear witness.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمنى، فانشق القمر، فأخذت فرقة خلف الجبل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says he saw the mountain through the opening between the two parts of the moon.
rows.anchor: عن الأسود، عن عبد الله قال: «رأيت الجبل من فرج القمر حين انشق»

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh called the split magic, asked travelers who confirmed seeing it, and then the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله قال

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: In his sermon, Hudhayfa says the Hour is near and the moon has split; today is the racecourse, tomorrow the contest, with Paradise the prize and the Fire the destination.
rows.anchor: وكان عطاء يروي أنه حذيفة فقال في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Mutim reports that the moon split while he and others were with the Messenger in Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم، عن أبيه قال: «انشق القمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon split in the time of the Messenger, before the Hijra, and that people saw its two halves.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قال: «انشق القمر قبل الهجرة»

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the split happened at Mecca during the Prophet's time; the polytheists turned away and called it persistent magic.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the people saw the moon split; in fuller reports, one half remained while the other went behind a mountain, and the Prophet called witnesses, including Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر}

rows.speaker: رجل
rows.claim: An unnamed man preaching in Mada'in recites the verse and urges listeners to prepare for the race of deeds: Paradise is the goal and the Fire the end.
rows.anchor: قدم رجل المدائن فقام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada invokes the verse to affirm that God brings about whatever He wills in His creation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر} [القمر: 1]

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign and the moon split twice in Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: «سأل أهل مكة النبي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the split had already occurred in Mecca during the Prophet's time; the polytheists turned away and called it magic.
rows.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وانشق القمر} [القمر: 1]

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says the moon's splitting at Mecca has already passed.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: «مضى انشقاق القمر بمكة»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the human created as Adam.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: { خلق الإنسان} [النحل: 4]

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes الإنسان to mean all people, with the singular form standing for the whole human kind, as in the statement that humanity is in loss.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بذلك الناس جميعا، وإنما وحد في اللفظ لأدائه عن جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari judges both Adam and humanity generally plausible, since the wording's apparent sense permits either; he cites the generic singular in 103:2.
rows.anchor: والقولان كلاهما غير بعيدين من الصواب لاحتمال ظاهر الكلام إياهما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God taught people to distinguish worldly and afterlife matters, including the lawful and unlawful, as evidence against them.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {علمه البيان} [الرحمن: 4]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In another wording, Qatada says البيان shows people good and evil and what to do or leave.
rows.anchor: أبو العوام، عن قتادة، في قوله: {علمه البيان}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses البيان as speech.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {علمه البيان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari holds that God taught people all the expression and knowledge they need for religion and worldly life, including lawful and unlawful matters, livelihoods, and speech; the unrestricted wording is general.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن يقال: معنى ذلك أن الله علم الإنسان ما به الحاجة إليه من أمر دينه ودنياه

rows.speaker: أبو رزين وسعيد
rows.claim: Abu Razin and Said say the prostration of the star and tree is their shadows prostrating.
rows.anchor: عن زبرقان، عن أبي رزين، وسعيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says every created thing sent down from heaven worships God, willingly or unwillingly.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والنجم والشجر يسجدان} [الرحمن: 6]

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the star and tree prostrate in the morning and evening.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {والنجم والشجر يسجدان} [الرحمن: 6]

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic commonly uses a singular verb with paired nonhuman collective nouns, as in sheep and cattle or palms and lote trees; using a dual verb is also permissible.
rows.anchor: وقد زعم الفراء أن العرب إذا جمعت الجمعين من غير الناس مثل السدر والنخل، جعلوا فعلهما واحدا
